abstract.p: A method for the numerical reconstruction of digital holograms which allows simultaneously amplitude and quantitative phase contrast imaging. The reconstruction method computes the propagation of the field that would be diffracted by the hologram during a standard hologram reconstruction. The method requires the adjustment of several reconstruction parameters for the definition of a digital replica of the reference wave. The method includes a digital method for the correction of the phase aberrations. The method can be used to reconstruct a set of holograms taken in different conditions. The method can be used to reconstruct several images from a single hologram taken with more than one reference waves and/or more than one object waves.

L'invention concerne un procédé pour la reconstruction numérique d'hologrammes numériques permettant l'imagerie à contraste de phases d'amplitude et quantitative simultanées. Ce procédé de reconstruction calcule la propagation du champ qui serait diffracté par l'hologramme au cours d'une reconstruction d'hologramme standard. Ce procédé requiert le réglage de plusieurs paramètres de reconstruction en vue de définir une réplique numérique de l'onde de référence. Ce procédé est formé d'un procédé numérique permettant la correction d'aberrations de phase et peut être utilisé pour reconstruire un ensemble d'hologrammes pris selon différentes conditions. Il peut également servir à reconstruire plusieurs images à partir d'un seul hologramme pris avec plus d'une onde de référence et/ou plus d'une onde objet.

description.p: METHOD AND APPARATUS FOR SIMULTANEOUS AMPLITUDE AND QUANTITATIVE PHASE CONTRAST IMAGING BY NUMERICAL RECONSTRUCTION OF DIGITAL HOLOGRAMS
RECONSTRUCTION OF DIGITAL HOLOGRAMS
Field of the invention
The present invention relates to a method for simultaneous amplitude and quantitative phase contrast imaging by numerical reconstruction of digitally encoded holograms
Discussion of the Background
The idea of recording a hologram of the specimen and reconstructing the hologram with a numerical method has been proposed for the first time in 1967 by J.W. Goodman and
R.W. Laurence, "Digital image formation from electronically detec.ed holograms.*' Appl.
Phys. Lett. 11, 77-79 (1967) who used a vidicon detector for the hciogram recording, and in
1971 by M.A. Kronrod et al.. "Reconstruction of a hologram with a computer," Soviet Phys.-
Technical Phys. 17, 333-334 (1972) who used a digitized image of a hologram recorded on a photographic plate. In these two references, the holograms were recorded in the holographic

Fourier configuration for which amplitude contrast images of the specimen can be numerically reconstructed by simply calculating the modulus of the two-dimensional Fourier transform of the hologram. A recent development using a Charged Coupled Device (CCD) camera as recording device, also in the Fourier configuration, has been patented (U.S. Pat.

4,955,974 and U.S. Pat. 5,214.531) and reported by W.S. Haddad et al. "Fourier-transform holographic microscope," Applied Optics 31. 4973-4978 (1992), and by K. Boyer et al.
"Biomedical three-dimensional holographic microimaging at vsible. ultraviolet and X-ray wavelength." Nature Medicine 2. 939-941 ( 1996), for X-ray amplitude contrast imaging of biological specimens

In 1994. on the basis of precedent works about digital holography (L P i aroslavsku and N S Merzlyakov, Methoαs of Digital Holography, Consultants Bureau. New York. 1980), Schnars et al. "Direct recording of holograms by a CCD target and numerical reconstruction." Applied Optics 33. 179-181 (1994), have reported the first numeπcally reconstructed amplitude contrast image from an off-axis hologram recorded in the Fresnel holographic configuration with a CCD camera. With the same reconstruction algonthm but wi h a low-coherence light source. E. Cuche et al "Optical Tomography at the Microscopic scale by means of a Numeπcal Low Coherence Holographic Technique." Proceedings SPEE on Optical and Imaging techniques for Bioimaging, Vienna. Vol. 2927. 61-66 ( 1996). have reported an application of numerical holography for tomographic imaging An application in micro-endoscopy, using also a Fresnel calculation for the hologram reconstruction, has been reported by O Coquoz et al ''Performances of endoscopic holography with a multicore optical fiber," Applied Optics 34. 7186-7193 (1995).

All the above mentioned works concern amplitude contrast imaging ror which only the modulus of the numerically reconstructed optical field is considered. The first use of a numeπcally reconstructed phase distπbution. from a Fresnel hologram, has Deεn reported by Schnars et al "Direct phase determination in hologram interferometry with use of digitally recorded holograms," J.Opt.Soc Am. A 11, 2011-2015 (1994), for an apphcation in holographic interferometry As presented in Ref Schnars et al., the used reconstruction algonthm is the same as for amplitude contrast imaging and do not really allows phase
contrast imaging, because, in this case, the reconstructed optic J field is the product of the object wave by the complex conjugate of the reference wave (or the product of the complex conjugate of the object wave by the reference wave). However, this reconstruction algonthm can be used in holographic interferometry. because the subtraction between two reconstructed phase distπbutions obtained with the same reference wave provides an image which represents only the phase difference between the deformed and undeformed states of the object.

The first example of a numencally reconstructed phase contrast image has been reported in 1997 by E. Cuche et al "Tomographie optique par une technique d'holographie numenque en faible coherence." J Opt. 28. 260-264 ( 1997), who have used a modified reconstruction algonthm including a multiplication of the digital hologram by a digital replica of the reference wave (digital reference wave). In Ref. Cuche et al.. the phase contrast image has been obtained with a plane wave as reference and in direct observation, meaning that no magnification or demagnification optics is introduced along the optical path of the object wave.
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION In companson with existing methods for phase contrast microscopy, such as the Zernicke or the Nomarski methods, the present invention provides a straightforward link
between phase contrast imaging and optical metrology.

"Quantitative phase contrast" means that the phase contrast image is free of artifacts or aberrations and can be directly used for quantitative measurements of optical properties (e g refractive index) or structural informations (e g. topography, thickness). More precisely,
"quantitative phase contrast" means here that the value of each pixel of the phase contrast image is equal, modulo 2π. to the value of the phase of the object wave at the corresponding area of specimen

'Simultaneous amplitude and quantitative phase contras ' means that two images ot the specimen can be reconstructed from the same hologram One of these images with an amplitude contrast and the other one with a quantitative phase contrast These images can be. analyzed separately or compared the one with the other Their information content (or the information content of several pairs of images reconstructed tor different onentations of the specimen) can be associated in order to build a computed three-dimensional descπption of the specimen, for example a three-dimensional tomography of semι-*ranspαrent specimens In the same way, the information content of several pairs of images reconstructed tor different wavelengths of the illuminating source can be associated in order to build a computed three- dimensional descnption of the specimen, for example a three-dimensional tomography of semi-transparent specimens, by application of the diffraction tomography techniques Such multi-wavelength proceαures can also be useful for the precise determination of objects dimensions or refractive index for metrologic applications Specrroscopic measurements are also possible with the present invention by recording two or more nolograms of the same specimen at different wavelengths

In companson with standard interference microscopy techniques which also provides simultaneously amplitude and quantitative pnase contrasts the ad\antage of the present invention is that the recording of only one hologram is necessary while the recording of four or more interferograms is required with interference microscopy Moreover, no displacement or moving of optical elements is needed with the present invention As a consequence, the
acquisition time is reduced providing α lower sensitivity to thei nal and mechanical drifts In pαrticulαr.pulsed sources, in particular pulsed laser sources and fast gated camera can be used to reduce acquisition time Robustness is a great assess of the present invention An other important advantage of the present invention m compαπson with interference microscopy is that the phase aberrations ore corrected digitally Indeed, a microscope objective which is introduced in an interferometer produces a curvature of the wavefronts which affects the phase of the object wave Therefore, for phase contrast imaging with the present invention or more generally in any interferometπc system, this phase aberration must corrected. In interference microscopy, this problem is solved expenmentally by inserting the same microscope objective in the reference arm, at equal distance from the exit of the interferometer This arrangement called Linnick interferometer requires that if any change has to be made in the object arm. then the same cnange must be precisely reproduced in the reference arm m such a way that the interference occurs between similarly deformed wavefronts As a consequence the expeπmental configuration requires a very high degree of precision An other possibility (Mirrau mterferomeiry) consists in magnifying the interference pattern. However, it is difficult to achieve high resolution imaging with this technique because a mimatuπzed interferometer must be inserted between the sample and the microscope oojective The present invention proposes a purely digital method which allows us to perform the correction by multiplying the reconstructed wavefront
with the computed complex conjugate of the phase aberration.

Depending on the configuration used for the recording of the hologram, the physical interpretation of amplitude and quantitative phase contrasts vary If the hologram is recorded w ith the wave that is reflected by the specimen (reflection geometry), the amplitude contrast
depends on vaπations of the reflectance at the specimen surface and the phase contrast depends on the topography of the specimen and/or on changes of the phase shift at the reflection If the hologram is recorded with the wave that is transmitted by α transparent or semi-transparent specimen (transmission geometry), the amplitude contrast is related to 5 changes in absorption and the phase contrast depends on vaπations of the thickness and/or of the refractive index (or more generally on vanations of the optical path)

In most cases, quantitative measurements of optical properties or structural informations, on the basis of phase measurements is ambiguous because phase contrast generally has more than one oπgin. For example, the measurement of the refractive index of

10 a transparent specimen requires the knowledge of the thickness and inversely the measurement of the thickness requires the knowledge of the refractive index. For topographic measurements with specimens composed of different mateπals. the analysis of the results must take into account the vaπation of the phase change on the reflection interface, if the complex index of refraction of the different mateπals is not the same If a pure - topographic or a pure refractive index or a pure thickness measurement is desired, known methods such as elhpsometry or multi-wavelength measurements could be used m combination with the present invention In particular, refractive index measurement on a transparent specimen of unknown thickness can be performed by recording two or more holograms at different wavelengths. Assuming that the thickness of the specimen is constant

">Q for each hologram, vaπations of the reconstructed phase distπbutions are due to vaπations of the refractive index as a function of the wavelength. Using a model descπbmg the vaπation of the refractive index as a function of the wavelength, the refracti e index of the specimen or its thickness can be deduced from the quantitative phase contrast images. With a semi-
transparent specimen (e.g biological cells or tissues) or more generally with α 3D scene composed of several reflective elements located at different depth, if a gating technique is used, such as time or coherent gating, the hologram can be recorded, in the reflection geometry, with the light that is reflected by a selected slice mside the specimen. In this case. both contrasts (amplitude and phase) depend on the optical properties of the selected slice and on the optical properties of other volumes inside the specimen where the light has travelled before and after the reflection.

The present invention provides a more general method for the numeπcal reconstruction of both amplitude and quantitative phase contrast images from a digital hologram. The numeπcal method for the hologram reconstruction compnses the calculation of a digital replica of the reference wave called digital reference wave An array of complex numbers called digital phase mask is also calculated in order to correct the phase aberrations of the imaging system.

The present invention provides unique results. The technique provides a quantitative phase contrast meaning that the reconstructed phase distπbution can be directly used for applications in metrology, m particular for surface profilometry. refractive index measurements or more generally for quantitative matenal testing (snape and position measurements, surface roughness measurement, optical properties measurement) Moreover, an amplitude contrast image of the specimen can be reconstructed from the same hologram. It is an important feature of the present invention that a three dimensional descπption of the specimen can be obtained digitally with only one image acquisition

The possibility of instantaneous acquisition of the amplitude and of the quantitative phase with a pulsed source or a time gated camera is a great advantage of the present
invention

Basically, the numeπcal reconstruction method performs a calculation which descnbes the propagation of the wavefront that would be diffracted by the hologram dunng a standard holographic reconstruction. The calculation consists in a numeπcαl evaluation of 5 the diffraction pattern which is produced in an observation plane when the hologram is illuminated by a replica of the reference wave. The scalar descπption of the diffraction is considered and the reconstruction method consists in the numeπcal calculation of the Fresnel- Kirchhoff integral or of the Rayleigh-Sommerfeld integral Depending on the configuration used for the hologram creation, the diffraction calculation can be performed using an 10 approximation of these integrals such as the Fraunhofer or the Fresnel integrals In some cases such as Fouπer holography, a simple Founer transform calculation can be used.

In a preferred manner, the configuration used for :ne hologram creation, in particular the distance between the hologram and the specimen, is adjusted in such a way to produce a Fresnel hologram for which the diffraction calculation can be performed in the Fresnel 1 *> approximation. The advantage of the Fresnel approximation is that the computations are simple and can be performed very fast using a discrete formulation of the Fresnel integral expressed m terms of a Fouπer transform. In addition, a w ide range of experimental configurations are covered by the Fresnel approximation

An important feature of the present invention is that image reconstruction, in both amplitude and phase contrast, requires the adjustment of several constants hich are involved by the numeπcal reconstruction method These constants are called reconstruction parameters and their values are defined by the expeπmental configuration. The reconstruction parameters can be divided into three categoπes. the reconstruction distance
which is related to image focusing: the reference wave parameters which are related to the definition of the digital reference wave, and the aberration correction parameters which are related to the definition of the digital phase mask It is an object of the present invention to descπbe how these reconstruction parameters are defined and how their values must be 5 adjusted. It is clear that the values of the reconstruction parameters are fixed for a given expeπmental configuration and that the same values of the reconstruction parameters can be used to reconstruct several holograms without new adjustment procedures if the expeπmental configuration is the same for these holograms.

Other parameters such as the wavelength, the detector size and the number of pixels 10 are requested by the numeπcal reconstruction method but these parameters have, in general, constant values and do not require a special adjustment.

An apparatus is disclosed, which make use of the different aspects of the method for simultaneaous amplitude and quantitative phase contrast imaging by numeπcal reconstruction of digital holograms. Depending on the size and accessibility of the object, three different l "5 implementations of the apparatus are disclosed: Numencal Holographic Telescope (NΗT), Numencal Holographic Microscope (NHM) and finally Numeπcal Holographic Endoscope (NHE)

DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE IN .ΕNTIQN
The embodiments of the present invention will be descnbed m more details with reference to the drawings.

FIG 1 shows diagrammaticaily the different steps of the entire imaging procedure The beam emitted by an illumination source 1 illuminates α set-up 2 which creates a hologram 4 of the specimen 3 The set-up 2 collects the light from the illumination source 1 and provides illumination 1 of the specimen 3 , it includes also a device for creating a reference wave R and a device for creating an object wave 0 from the light that is transmitted or reflected or scattered by the specimen 3 The object wave 0 and the reference wave R are combined in such a way that they interfere in a plane
The interference between the reference wave R and the object wave O creates the hologram 4 which can be descnbed as a two-dimensional distπbution of intensity
where R~" and O* are the complex conjugates of the reference and object waves respectively

The present invention is not restπcted to the optical domain and can be applied for the numeπcal reconstruction of holograms recorded with any kind of electromagnetic (e g X-ray) or non-electromagnetic (e.g. acoustics or heats) waves. Photon density waves can also be used. For this reason, the nature, the wavelength and the coherence of the illumination source 1 are not specified here Gas lasers, semiconductor lasers, solid state lasers, laser diodes, superluminescent diodes, narrow and broadband sources, white light sources, piezoelectric transducers, X-ray sources, and electron beam are examples of means which can be used as
illumination source

A combination of two or more illumination sources can also be used For example, two illumination sources of different wavelengths can be combined in order to create an illumination source with a so called synthetic wavelength

In a preferred manner, the set-up 2 is designed in such α way that the polanzation of the reference wave R matches (as close as possible) the polanzation of the object wave O This closeness of the polanzation of the object to that of the reference waves is important to optimize the interference between these two waves. If the object wave contains different kind of photons with different polanzation states, as it happens for example when scattenng events occur side the specimen or when the birefπngence of the specimen is not uniform, working with a fixed polanzation of the reference wave allows one to select the photons of the object wave, the polanzation of which is close to the polanzation of the reference wave

The device which creates the object wave O can include magnifications optics or demagmfication optics. Direct imaging, without any optics between the specimen and the plane where the hologram is created, is also possible

The term "magnification optics" is to be understood as being a single lens or an assembly of lenses and/or optical fibers which produces a magnified image of the specimen with a better resolution than direct imaging The case of a magnification optics producing an image of the SDecimen. the size of which is the same as the size of the specimen
(magnification equal to unity), is also included here.

The term ''demagmfication optics" is to be understood as being a single lens or an assembly of lenses and optical fibers which produces a smaller image of the specimen in order to allow imaging of larger specimens than direct imaging.
In a preferred manner, the set-up 2 will be designed in u/der to produce an off-axis hologram. The term "off-axis hologram" is to be understood as meaning that the directions of propagation of the reference wave R and of the object wave 0 are not parallel, at their incidence on the plane where the hologram is created The off-axis geometry advantageously permits to separate the zero order of diffraction, the real image and the twin image dunng the reconstruction. Several configurations can be used for the creation of an off-axis hologram. FIG. 2A presents one of the possible configurations with an angle θ between the directions of the object wave and of the reference wave reference at their incidence on the hologram plane

Depending on the resolution of the media used for hologram recording, the off-axis geometry may be restπcted to small angles in order to avoid that the spatial frequency of the created lnterferogram exceeds the resolution power of recording media In other words, the angle between the reference wave and the object wave, at their incidence on the plane where the hologram is created, must not exceed a certain value for which the interference fπnges of the hologram are not resolved by the image acquisition system. The off-axis geometry may even be considered at the limit of very small angles, but in this case, the zero order of diffraction may cover parts or integrality of the twin image or of the real image. In this case, additional methods can be used in order to suppress the zero order of diffraction For example, a method proposed by TM Kreis and WP O Juptner . "Suppression of the dc term in digital holography," Opt. Eng 36. 2357-2360 (1997) can be applied oefore the numencal reconstruction However, this method, which consists in subtracting the mean intensity from the digital hologram permits only the elimination of the so-called dc term of the zero order of diffraction from the reconstructed images In other words, if a reference wave of constant amplitude (for example a plane wave) is used for the hologram creation, the
method proposed by.M. Kreis and W PO Juptner reference can be descnbed as being a method which produces a hologram of the following form:
As a consequence, the object component of the zero order of diffraction ( 0\~). which is in general not constant the hologram plane, is not suppressed by this method.

We propose here a method for the complete elimination of the zero-order of diffraction. In pπnciple, this method can also be applied when the amplitude of the reference wave is not constant. In a general way, this method can be descnbed as being a method which produces a hologram which contain only the lnter eπng terms of the hologram
IH(x. y) = R"0 RO" .

Such a result can be obtained by subtracting a locally evaluated value of the zero order of diffraction (|R|~ +\0\~) form the digital hologram. For example, the digital hologram can be divided in small elements called submatnx of constant (or non-constant) sizes, and the method proposed by T.M. Kreis and W.P O Juptner reference can be applied to each of these submatnx. The size and the number of the submatnx must be chosen in such a way to restore, with enougn precision, the vanations of the zero order of diffraction in the hologram plane. However the size of a submatnx must not be smaller than a minimum size for which a submatnx contains only one constructive and one destructive interference.

Another aspect of the present invention is based on the application of a band-pass filter to the Fouπer transform of the digital hologram, and which also allows for the complete elimination of the zero-order of diffraction This method is based on the fact tnat, in off-axis
holography, the spatial frequencies corresponding the interfeπng terms (R"*0 and RO*) are higher than the spatial frequencies which correspond to the zero order of diffraction (\R\2 As a consequence, we propose to apply, optionally, before the numencal reconstruction of the digital hologram, a digital image processing method which includes the steps of
- computing the two dimensional (2D) discrete Founer transform of the digital hologram,
- locating, in the Fouπer transform of the digital hologram, the spatial frequencies which correspond to the interfeπng terms R*0 and RO*

- computing the multiplication of the Fouπer transform of the hologram by a 2D function which eliminates or attenuates the spatial frequencies which do not correspond to the interfeπng terms This operation removes (or attenuates) the spatial frequencies which correspond to the zero order of diffraction and can also remove other parasitic spatial frequencies,
- computation of the discrete inverse Fouπer transform.

At this step, as a consequence of the suppression of the low spatial frequencies of the hologram, a filtered digital hologram ith a constant zero order is obtained Tne value of the zero order is equal to the mean intensity calculated for the entire hologram area. Therefore. the zero order can be completelv suppressed bv subtracting the mean mtensitv to the intensity each pixel of the filtered digital hologram

With reference to FIG. l, the application of the above mentioned Founer filteπng image processing is one of the possible digital image processing which can be optionally applied before and/or after the numeπcal reconstruction of the hologram At tπis step, several
digital image processing treatments can be applied in order to improve the signal to noise ratio or in order to enhance the fringes visibility of the digital hologram 7 For example bπghtness and contrast adjustment, offset subtraction, modification of the distnbution of grav leveis. thresholding, application of phase unwrapping methods to the quantitative phase contrast image, application of histogram equalization, application of two-dimensional high- pass spatial frequency filters or low-pass spatial frequency filters, application of one or several two-dimensional band-pass spatial frequency filters, application of statistical operations on a set of several images, application of image processing treatment in order to suppress the zero order of diffraction and/or the twin image and/or the real image It is also possible to increase or to decrease the number of pixels of the digital hologram The digital hologram can also be multiplied by a two-dimensional function (for example a Hanning or a Hamming or a Gaussian window) in order to perform data windo ing This feature of a possible digital image processing treatment of the hologram is one of the advantage of the present invention in compaπson with standard holographic methods which use. for example, photographic plates as recording media and which do not allow for such a straightfor ard processing of the hologram, before its reconstruction

A particularly interesting digital treatment consists in multiplying the hologram by a two- dimensional real function which modifies the transmission (or the amplitude transrmttance) of the hologram aperture in order to perform an apodization of this aperture Aperture apodization is a well known technique in optics and is used to reduce diffraction effects

(fluctuations of the diffracted field in amplitude and phase) aπsing when a beam of coherent lignt is truncated by an aperture An apocized aperture is charactenzed by an amplitude transrmttance (transmission) which does not change abruptly from zero to unity at the edge of
the aperture, but in a smooth and continuous manner. Several kind of continuous functions can be used to define the transition of the transmission (from zero to unity) at the edges of the aperture Gaussian. super-Gaussian, tπgonometnc or a combination of functions A transmissiπon function defined using an interpolated function can also be used An transmis- sion fonction defined iterαtively dunng an optimization process can also be used In a preferred manner, the transmission function of the apodized aperture is defined m such a way that a large region in the center of the aperture remains transparent

Assuming that with off-axis holography the zero order of diffraction corresponds to low spatial frequencies, its suppression can also be performed expenmentally by spatially filtenng the hologram 4 before acquisition of the image This operation can be performed using a non linear optical element like a photo refractive crystal combined with a so-called4-/ system composed of two lenses of focal length/with a high-pass mask located in the Fouπer plane of the first lens With reference to FIG 2B, such a 4-/system can be considered as being an example of said optional optical elements which can be inserted between the beam splitter and the image acquisition

The extreme case of in-line or Gabor holograms can also be considered with the present invention In this case the present invention can be used combination with otner methods (image processing methods or expeπmental procedures) for the elimination of the zero order of diffraction and/or for the elimination of the twin or real image For example, a method which is similar to interference microscopy has been proposed by I Yamaguchi and

T Zhang, "Phase-shifting digital holography". Opt Lett. 22, 1268-1270 (1997). This method requires the recording of four interferograms taken with phase shifts (of 90°) of the reference wave and allows the suppression of both the zero order of diffraction and the twin
image In this case, or more generally when a procedure is used to shift or to modulate the phase of the reference wave and/or the phase of the object wave, the object wave can be measured in amplitude and phase tn the hologram plane The present invention can then be used in order to recover the amplitude and the phase at the surrace of the specimen. Piezo 5 actuated mirrors, acousto-optics or electro-optics or photo-elαstic modulators are example of optional optical elements which can be used to modulate or to shift the phase of the reference wave and/or of the object wave

For a heterodyne detection, said means which creates the reference wave R can include a device which modifies the wavelength of the reference wave with respect to the wavelength of 0 the object wave A similar device can also be inserted in said means which creates an object wave 0 Acousto optic modulators, electro-optic modulators, photo-elastic modulators, piezo- electπc dnven mirrors are example of means which can be used to modulate the wavelength of the reference wave and/or of the object wave These means are examples of optional optical components featured in FIGS. 2B, 2C and 2D Physically distinct sources can also be used for ^ the illumination and for the creation of the reference

In a preferred manner, the set-up 2 will be designed in order to produce a Fresnel hologram The term "Fresnel hologram ' is to be understood as meaning that the hologram reconstruction can be performed by a calculation of scalar diffraction in the Fresnel approximation. The numencal calculation of the discrete Fresnel integral will be explained in 0 details further The advantage of the Fresnel approximation is that the computations are simple and can be performed very fast. In addition, a wide range of expeπmental configurations are covered by the Fresnel approximation
